corrections.entity_description: Koninklijke Philips N.V., Dutch electronics company headquartered in Eindhoven (Wikidata Q170416)
corrections.reason: local-knowledge inference by the project owner: the road in Maarheeze heads to the A2 and connects to the Eindhovenseweg, i.e. toward Eindhoven where Philips was headquartered (Strijp), and the buurt is an industrial estate (Den Engelsman/Rondven); an inference, not a documented naming record

corrections.entity_description: German-born officer in Dutch service (1766-1823), led the Indies Brigade at Waterloo
corrections.reason: local-knowledge candidate from the Eindhoven review sheet; checked: a Dutch general of that name exists and the Generalenbuurt also names Chasse (Waterloo/Antwerp era) and other 19th-century generals. Not a documented naming record.

corrections.entity_description: Dutch cavalry officer (1774-1851), helped found the cavalry of the Kingdom of the Netherlands
corrections.reason: local-knowledge candidate from the Eindhoven review sheet; checked: a general of that name existed and the Generalenbuurt names several 19th-century generals. Not a documented naming record.

corrections.entity_description: Dutch politician, minister and later mayor of Eindhoven (1903-1984)
corrections.reason: review sheet; verified on Wikipedia that Kolfschoten was burgemeester of Eindhoven; the Engelsbergen theme is Eindhoven mayors

corrections.entity_label: Josephus Theodorus Maria Smits van Oyen
corrections.entity_description: Mayor of Eindhoven 1885-1898 and member of the Tweede Kamer (1858-1898)
corrections.reason: review sheet; verified on Wikipedia: mayor of Eindhoven; the Engelsbergen theme is Eindhoven mayors

corrections.entity_description: Dutch resistance victim (born 1921): worked at Philips in Eindhoven, tried to reach England as an Engelandvaarder, arrested in 1944
corrections.reason: review sheet; checked: Stichting 18 September lists him among Eindhoven's WWII victims, and Kerkdorp Acht has a cluster of local war-victim streets. Not a documented naming record.

corrections.entity_description: Wife of Anton Philips (1878-1970)
corrections.reason: review sheet ('very likely'); Philipsdorp is the Philips garden village and names the family; the Philips Museum page exists for her. Not a documented naming record.
review sheet (suspected): 'glas', the material behind Philips's light bulbs, in the Philips garden village; no person is asserted, only the kind
review sheet: 'luchthaven' means airport and the road is by Eindhoven Airport (sibling of Flight Lane); a common noun, not a person

corrections.entity_description: spice
corrections.reason: review sheet: 'kaneel' is cinnamon; the nearby Zoutstraat is salt (OSM Q11254), so a spice/trade theme, not a naval hero

corrections.entity_description: city in Noord-Brabant
corrections.reason: review sheet: a directional road toward Tilburg (<Place>seweg)

the earlier Wikidata match (painter Henriette Ronner-Knip) does not fit the Philips garden village and is withdrawn. Candidates: Anton Philips's wife Anne Henriette Elisabeth Maria de Jongh, his daughter Henriette Anna Philips (1906-2007, Wikidata Q76268707), or Frederik Philips's aunt Henriette Pressburg (Q19841721, less likely). The neighbouring streets honour the family (Frederiklaan = Frederik Philips, Elisabethlaan = his wife Maria Elisabeth Heijligers per OSM, Annastraat = Anton's wife). Unresolved, so only the kind is kept.
